content:
ana: Heads-up — we need to finalize TTLs and grace periods for metering claims before next rollout. Current behavior: claims expire immediately at window end which spikes invoice churn for slightly-late events. Proposal: add a server-side `grace_period_seconds` and a `soft_ttl` field so claims remain queryable for audits/backfill for N days.

mike: +1. rough Q: is `grace_period_seconds` per-claim or per-account? could do per-tenant override but keep a global default.

sophia: audit/backfill note: analysts rely on claims being immutable for 30d. If we make them soft-expire we must ensure audit index keeps canonical copies or snapshots. otherwise revert/blame becomes hard. :thinking_face: 

kevin: I think three concerns: 1) billing correctness 2) auditability 3) storage cost. tradeoffs: keep full canonical events for 90d (cold storage), expose soft TTL of 7d for normal queries, and a longer `provenance_ttl` for audit reads.

jordan: sketch of schema change (backwards compatible):
```json
{
  "claim_id": "uuid",
  "account_id": "acct_123",
  "window_start": 1700000000,
  "window_end": 1700003599,
  "tokens": 12345,
  "status": "finalized", // pending | finalized | expired
  "soft_ttl": 604800,        // seconds (7d) - visible in normal queries
  "provenance_ttl": 2592000, // seconds (30d) - kept for audits/backfill
  "grace_period_seconds": 3600 // allow late attributions within 1h of window_end
}
```

ana: (typo) ana: we need a migration path — old claims without fields should default to `soft_ttl=0` and `provenance_ttl=30d`. Also enforce server-side write that rejects `grace_period_seconds` > 7d unless tenant has override.

mike: operational question: how do we surface that to billing UI? Should invoices show a provisional section for claims in-grace? would reduce surprise.

sophia: yes — display `provisional` flag on line-items, show expected finalization timestamp, and only finalize after provenance window or explicit reconciliation. also emit `claim.finalized` webhook when status flips.

kevin: perf note: index strategy — keep a hot index for `status in (pending,finalized)` with `soft_ttl` eviction and a cold compressed archive keyed by `claim_id` for `provenance_ttl`. avoids scanning huge cold store for normal queries.

jordan: implementation TODOs: 1) storage layer TTL support + migration job 2) API: accept soft/provenance TTLs but validate 3) UI: provisional line-items 4) audit tools: snapshot exports for last-30d 5) billing job: wait for `grace_period_seconds` before final invoice commit (or mark provisional).

ana: sounds good. let's land a small RFC summary and a migration plan. I'll draft defaults: soft_ttl=7d, provenance_ttl=30d, grace_period_seconds=3600 global default. Will post RFC link in #eng-platform when ready. :memo:

sre-bot: deploy-bot: reminder — feature gates required, canary rollout recommended for 2 weeks. See <https://redwood.internal/deploys/metering-ttl>

mike: thanks — thumbs up. can we also add a metric `claims_finalized_lag_seconds` to watch regressions?

sophia: agreed, add alert if >95th percentile > 2h for any tenant.

ana: noted. I'll include metrics and alerting in the RFC. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
